subject: Request: temporary uptime waiver + monthly-credit anchoring for Private pilot
messages:
From: Nadia Romero <contracts@nimbusdata.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>
Cc: procurement@nimbusdata.com
Date: Sun, 8 Apr 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: SLA ask for Private pilot: uptime floor and monthly credit anchor

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the call yesterday — appreciated the technical overview and the Private deployment option.

As we scope the pilot (Q2) for our AI search layer, procurement/legal has a couple of asks we need to see in writing before we can sign:

- Temporary uptime floor: For the first 6 months of the Private pilot, Nimbus is asking to reduce the standard uptime % requirement in the SLA from 99.95% to 99.90% (to accommodate on-prem integration and initial load testing).
- Monthly credit anchor: If uptime in any calendar month falls below the agreed floor, we ask for an automatic credit equal to 8% of that month’s Redwood invoice for every 0.1% below the floor, up to a 25% monthly cap.
- Maintenance carveouts: We need explicit language around planned maintenance windows (48-hour rolling schedule, 30-day advance notice) and a carveout for agreed maintenance that does not count toward availability.

I’ve attached a one-page summary (Nimbus_SLA_ask_v1.pdf) with the above bullets for your legal team.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is open to a six-month conditional exception for the pilot with the credit anchor above? If so, legal will draft the amendment and we can share DocuSign.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Nadia Romero
Head of Contracts | Nimbus Data
attachments: Nimbus_SLA_ask_v1.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>
To: Nadia Romero <contracts@nimbusdata.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbusdata.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask for Private pilot: uptime floor and monthly credit anchor

Hi Nadia — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment. We’re excited about the pilot with Nimbus.

Short answer: we can be flexible but want to preserve predictable economics and operational guardrails for Redwood. High level proposal from our side:

- Conditional floor: Redwood can agree to a temporary 99.90% uptime floor for the first 6 months of a Private pilot, provided we jointly run a performance readiness checklist and agree on initial traffic shaping.

- Credit formula (alternative): instead of a linear 8% per 0.1% below floor (which scales quickly), we propose a banded approach to avoid outsized credits during early tuning:
  - Availability >= 99.90%: no credits
  - 99.60% <= Availability < 99.90%: credit = 6% of monthly invoice
  - 99.00% <= Availability < 99.60%: credit = 12% of monthly invoice
  - Availability < 99.00%: credit = 25% of monthly invoice (hard cap)

- Cap and duration: the cap would remain at 25% per month, and the exception would automatically revert to standard 99.95% after 6 months unless both parties agree to extend.

- Maintenance carveout: agree on planned maintenance windows; Redwood will provide a 30-day rolling calendar and coordinate a single 3-hour weekly maintenance window where possible. Anything outside that requires advance notice and will be excluded from availability calculations.

Next steps: I’m looping in Karthik (legal/contracts) and Laura (Customer Success / onboarding) to give more detail on the redline and operational checklist. If that approach looks reasonable, Karthik can provide an amendment template and Laura will work on the readiness checklist and a short runbook to be attached to the amendment.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call Wednesday 10:00–12:00 PT so we can confirm the details and timeline?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed-sla-amendment-20280410.docx

Marcus / Laura — quick legal/contract note (cc’ing Nadia to keep visibility):

1) Banding rationale: the banded credit approach Marcus proposed keeps early-stage credits predictable while giving Nimbus visible remediation paths. It also reduces the incentive to overclaim small degradations.

2) Proposed amendment language (short summary to include in redline):
   - "Temporary Availability Floor": The Parties agree that for the initial six (6) month Pilot Period the Availability commitment shall be 99.90%.
   - "Remedy Bands": For any calendar month during the Pilot Period, Remedies shall be calculated per the following bands: Availability >= 99.90%: 0% credit; 99.60%–99.89%: 6% credit; 99.00%–99.59%: 12% credit; <99.00%: 25% credit (monthly cap).
   - "Cap & Aggregation": Monthly caps apply per invoice period and will not be aggregated across months. Credits shall be applied to the next invoice cycle.
   - "Operational Prerequisites": Pilot commencement is conditioned on execution of a Performance Readiness Checklist and a joint traffic shaping plan.

3) Maintenance carveouts: we should narrow the "planned maintenance" window language. Suggest Redwood-provided 30-day calendar + 48-hour notice for scheduled changes that are expected to impact availability, and a separate emergency maintenance category (mutually agreed) that will be excluded only if both parties confirm emergency status within 24 hours.

4) DocuSign path: If Nimbus is comfortable, I can issue a short amendment redline (track changes) that references the main SOW and contains the performance checklist as an exhibit. I would expect one round of redlines.

Laura — once we have the greenlight, can you lead the readiness checklist and tag the internal infra owners?

Karthik
General Counsel (contracts lead) | Redwood Inference

Marcus / Karthik / Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed bands. The banded approach is acceptable to Nimbus as long as three items are explicit in the amendment:

1) Credits are automatic and apply to the next invoice (no dispute-shaped delays).
2) A clearly defined "Performance Readiness Checklist" is attached and signed off by the two technical leads before pilot start.
3) Emergency maintenance carveouts require joint confirmation within 24 hours and will be documented to avoid unilateral exclusions.

If you can circulate the redline with those points mirrored (Karthik’s summary looks right), I’ll run it through our GC and procurement and aim to return signed DocuSign within 72 hours.

We’re available for the Wednesday 10:30 PT call if that still works — I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Nadia Romero
Head of Contracts | Nimbus Data
